advisor_identified: Historian of science and professor of humanities at York University; supervisor of the Lorenz Oken dissertation reported in 2002.

evidence.says: York University’s 2001 faculty calendar lists Martin Fichman as a professor of humanities in Arts and gives his MA and PhD as Harvard degrees (abbreviated Harv.).
Harvard’s Ph. D. Theses in the History of Science By Year, page 2, lists Fichman, Martin under 1969 with the title French Stahlism and 18th Century Chemistry.

The indexed text of York’s Gazette of April 17, 2002 reports a completed York history doctorate on Lorenz Oken and the institutionalization and professionalization of science, naming humanities professor Martin Fichman as its thesis supervisor.
The University of Chicago Press author page identifies Martin Fichman as a professor of humanities at York University.

notes: The advisor’s Harvard PhD is independently confirmed by York; Harvard supplies the year and dissertation title. These match the linked record’s author, institution, department, year and title, with only hyphenation differing in the title. The Gazette identification was available in search-indexed text; direct retrieval returned an error.
